newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila waterworks privatisation cleared by court.
newsitem.headline: Manila waterworks privatisation cleared by court.

text.p: The Philippine Court of Appeals on Wednesday lifted an order restraining President Fidel Ramos from proceeding with the privatisation of Manila's water system, clearing the way for the signing of contracts.
The three-judge court dismissed for "lack of merit" a petition by a group led by former Defence Secretary Lisandro Abadia to stop Ramos from carrying out the programme.

The court, in a nine-page decision, upheld a ruling by the Manila regional trial court that Abadia's group failed to show "irreparable injury" should the court not stop the government from privatising the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS).

"With the decision, there is no more legal impediment for the President to act on the recommendation of the Committee on Privatisation to award the concession agreements to the winning bidders," Presidential legal counsel Rene Cayetano said in a statement.
The government had offered two 25-year concessions to run the city's waterworks system.
The consortium of Ayala Corp, Bechtel Corp of the United States and United Utilities won the east zone concession.
The west zone was won by Benpres Holdings with France's Lyonnaise des Eaux SA.
Abadia's group had said Ramos' authority to privatise the MWSS lapsed in December 1995 and the government therefore had no right to go ahead with the deal.
But the Court of Appeals said the issue on whether Ramos was authorised to privatise MWSS was still pending resolution before a lower court.
The waterworks privatisation has been dogged by controversy as another group representing MWSS employees has gone to court saying the move would affect their jobs.
